extracted.intended_audience: NLP and AI researchers, practitioners, and engineers working on LLM-based patent-document generation and evaluation; patent analytics researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and generating patent abstracts from the first claim using large language models (LLMs) under controlled prompting, perturbation, and downstream-task evaluations. The benchmark focuses on measuring semantic fidelity, robustness, stylistic properties, and domain utility across CPC subclasses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task formulation: abstract from first claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate the patent abstract given the first claim of the patent. The benchmark's main objective is generating abstract given the first claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first claim is used as the input because it ‘defines the scope of protection’ and concisely summarizes the invention’s key elements; framework can be extended to other inputs/outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero-shot prompting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the model only a task description without any examples to test the model's generalization based on pretraining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example prompt: 'You are a patent expert. Given the following patent claim, write an informative abstract that captures the key invention, technical purpose, and functionality.' Measures baseline generalization ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Few-shot prompting
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a small number of input-output examples to condition the model on desired output format and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use three claim-abstract pairs as examples (chosen with varying lengths and performance levels: high, medium, low NLP scores) to improve coherence, structure, and adherence to domain-specific language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly instruct the model to reason step-by-step before producing the final abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt asks the model to 'first analyze it step by step to identify the key invention, its technical purpose, and how it functions. Then, based on this reasoning, write a formal abstract.' Helps tasks needing reasoning and yields higher ROUGE/BLEU in experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input perturbation techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply realistic perturbations to input claims to simulate noisy/imperfect user inputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques used: (i) Typographical errors via simulated keyboard typos; (ii) BERT-based contextual substitutions that replace words with contextually appropriate alternatives; (iii) Random swaps of adjacent words. Examples provided in Appendix A.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness under perturbations
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure consistency and stability of generated abstracts when input claims are perturbed (typos, contextual replacements, word swaps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether model outputs produce only modest drops in NLP metrics (BLEU, ROUGE) and maintain semantic quality (BERTScore/Cosine). Strong models should be resilient to realistic minor disturbances.

rubrics_metrics.name: BERTScore (semantic similarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use BERTScore to evaluate semantic similarity between generated text and reference abstract using contextual embeddings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as the major evaluation measure to preserve context accuracy, coherence, and preciseness. In experiments, BERTScore >= 0.85 indicates strong alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUGE-L (longest common subsequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ROUGE-L to assess longest common subsequence (LCS) between generated and reference text, computing precision, recall, and F1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures sequence-level overlap and some semantic coherence; CoT prompting increased ROUGE in experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: BLEU (n-gram overlap)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure n-gram overlap between generated and reference text to assess surface-level similarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originally for MT; correlates to some extent with human judgment but is weaker for semantic evaluation. Useful to capture literal overlap differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cosine similarity (vector similarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute cosine similarity between vector representations of generated and reference texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures global embedding-based similarity; used alongside BERTScore to capture semantic alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain-based evaluation — Patent classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Test usefulness of generated abstracts by classifying them into CPC subclasses and comparing classifier performance against original abstracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplify multi-label CPC classification to single-label per-experiment setting for comparison. Fine-tune a transformer-based classifier and report accuracy, precision, recall, F1 to identify disparities between original and generated abstracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating classification downstream task, report accuracy, precision, recall, and F1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fine-tune a Sentence-Transformer encoder (e.g., all-MiniLM-L12-v2) with fixed hyperparameters (example: LR=2e-5, batch_size=16, epochs=4) and use those standard metrics to compare generated vs original abstracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain-based evaluation — Patent retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether generated abstracts retrieve a similar set of patents as the original abstracts when used as queries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed abstracts with Sentence-BERT (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), compute cosine similarities, rank documents, and quantify overlap using overlap@k (k=5,10,25) and Spearman rank correlation; include a randomized baseline to measure beyond-chance performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrieval evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure retrieval similarity using overlap@k and Spearman rank correlation, comparing generated and original abstract retrieval results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also compare against a random/shuffled baseline. High overlap@k and Spearman indicate good semantic alignment in retrieval behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative measure — abstract length (verbosity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute abstract length (in tokens) to assess verbosity and structural compactness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer abstracts may capture more detail but risk redundancy; generated abstracts were longer on average (e.g., GPT-4o > Llama3 > human) and correlate more strongly with claim length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative measure — readability score
rubrics_metrics.description: Use readability metrics to evaluate linguistic complexity of generated text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher scores indicate more intricate sentence structures typical of technical writing; humans scored higher variability and higher mean readability than some LLM outputs in the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative measure — passive voice usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute percentage of passive voice usage as a stylistic feature common in patent writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure distribution and mean; human abstracts showed higher and more variable passive-voice use compared to more uniform LLM outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylistic analysis and variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess stylistic properties such as repetitiveness, templated phrasing, tone, and variability across outputs and compared to human-written abstracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for indicators that LLM outputs are more uniform, more repetitive, longer, and less readable than human texts; use this to argue for domain-specific fine-tuning to better replicate expert style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset construction and balancing
rubrics_metrics.description: Build the benchmark dataset from PatentsView: U.S. patents granted in 2022, extracting claim-abstract pairs and CPC subclass labels; retain CPC subclasses with >=1000 instances and sample ~1,000 instances per subclass for balanced coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include patent ID, title, abstract, and CPC label. Focus classes in the study: A61, G06, H04 and their relevant subclasses; resulting dataset ~21,000 records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental control: compare generated vs original abstracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Always evaluate generated abstracts against the original human-written abstracts using the same downstream pipelines and metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is to measure alignment and functional equivalence (classification/retrieval behavior), not to improve absolute task performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inference time and computational cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure and report model inference times and resource requirements as part of practical evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report hardware and runtime (e.g., LLaMA 3 took ~39 hours on NVIDIA H200 for full dataset; GPT-4o mini and GPT-4.1 were faster). Use these measurements to weigh trade-offs between speed, cost, and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding and model choices for downstream tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify encoder/embedding models and training hyperparameters used for classification and retrieval experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the paper: all-MiniLM-L12-v2 for classification (fine-tuned with LR=2e-5, batch 16, 4 epochs); all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for retrieval (max seq len 256, batch size 32). Document these choices to ensure reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt example selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Select few-shot examples with diversity in length and performance level to better condition the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use three examples chosen with varying lengths and varying NLP performance levels (high, medium, low) to teach desired output format and robustness across styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain utility criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated abstracts should preserve class-specific information and be functionally useful in patent analytics pipelines (classification, retrieval).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirically validate by showing generated abstracts lead to comparable or improved downstream task metrics relative to originals (as in classification and retrieval experiments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and legal constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that patent generation should not be fully automated and must comply with legal requirements and regulations of patent laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include human supervision in any patent-generation workflow and consider the legal/ethical implications of using LLM-generated patent text in filings.
